original.test: packages/engine/src/verification/engine-verification.test.ts: missing verification resumes the same native Run and publishes completion only after actual pass
original.failure: pendingApproval polled snapshots with setImmediate and asserted a pending approval within a 5 s wall-clock deadline; none was observed (test 5,427.9 ms).

findings.nearDeadlineOnHostedMac: The passing rerun took 5,580.8 ms, longer than the failing attempt, so the approval routinely arrives close to the 5 s helper deadline on hosted macOS under the 4-way test concurrency. Other tests in the file took 0.9-1.8 s there.
findings.busyPolling: setImmediate polling read about 19,500 snapshots in 750 ms; it added roughly 10% locally and is not the main cost.

gitProcesses.probe: Each RepositoryContextService.preview spawns 4 git processes in this unborn repository: check-ignore --no-index --stdin, rev-parse --verify HEAD, rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD, symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD.

previewCallers.note: two direct previews plus a re-observing query that previews twice

previewCallers.path: VerificationHostService.observe/source (controller evaluate, execution observation, run start, stop, before-provider)

findings.cause: The pre-approval path performs about 45 four-process git probes. Process spawning slows sharply on a loaded hosted macOS runner, which moves the approval to about 5 s; the fixed 5 s helper deadline then fails intermittently. The engine's behavior was correct in both attempts.

resolution.change: pendingApproval returns an already pending approval, otherwise waits for the next approval.requested event after its snapshot's lastSeq, raced against waitForRun. A Run that settles without an approval fails immediately with the snapshot's tools.
resolution.boundary: The wall-clock proxy (5 s) is replaced by the causal condition it approximated. The hang bound moved from the 5 s helper to each test's own timeout (20-25 s). A missing approval still fails, now as soon as the Run settles.
resolution.intermediateFailure: A first version subscribed from seq 0; the repair test's second wait then matched the earlier, already decided approval and failed 2/2 locally. Subscribing after the snapshot's lastSeq fixed it.

hostedAfterFix.note: The same test took 5.4-5.6 s before the change on hosted macOS; one run per OS does not establish the size of the improvement.

followUp: PERF-GIT-01: bounded reduction of repository-context git probes (for example one combined HEAD/branch probe, or reusing the query observation's own preview inside assertFresh) that preserves the never-bypass-fresh-check contract and passes the full gate.
